items.title: Sasha wanted to trace her genealogy. Instead she uncovered a 30-year-old mistake
items.description: When Sasha Szafranski matched with a stranger on a genealogy website, she uncovered an IVF mix-up that had been hidden for 30 years.

items.title: What you need to know about Iran today, with Matt Doran
items.description: The ABC's Middle East Correspondent Matt Doran is in Beirut and is providing daily updates on the Middle East war.

items.title: $30K drone reshapes how Australia and the world view future wars
items.description: Defence analysts say the early lessons of the Iran conflict are fairly clear: drone warfare is here to stay and Australia needs to rapidly improve its counter-drone capabilities.

items.title: Inside Venezuela, we saw why its vast oil reserves can't help the current crisis
items.description: Foreign Correspondent goes inside Venezuela's oil regions where boom towns have gone bust, leaving behind a shattered industry needing billions to reboot.

items.title: Live: Trump tells allies 'get involved quickly' in securing Strait of Hormuz
items.description: The US president hits out at European allies, who he says "weren't that enthusiastic" about helping, as Iranian drones and missiles closed the shipping channel. Follow live.

items.title: The chances of a rate rise have spiked from zero to 71pc
items.description: The market thinks the RBA is likely to lift interest rates today, with increasing uncertainty surrounding inflation as the Middle East war puts upward pressure on prices.

items.title: Why the RBA will add to the petrol pain
items.description: As Reserve Bank board members gather for the second day of meetings this morning, they already would have been peppered with dire warnings about the potential impact of the energy shock.

items.title: Seven in 10 employers admit excluding candidates due to illness or age
items.description: Seven in 10 employers have revealed they are excluding candidates in certain groups, including those who live with a long-term illness, disability, mental illness or are over 55, according to a new survey.

items.title: New laws for NSW after 'sickening' attacks on LGBTQIA+ teens
items.description: Offenders convicted of hate crimes against the LGBTQIA+ community in New South Wales could face up to seven years behind bars under new legislation being introduced to parliament.

items.title: Young people particularly vulnerable to cults post-COVID
items.description: According to one of Australia's leading cult experts, the number of young adults between 17 and 25 years old joining cults since COVID is increasing at an alarming rate.

items.title: Paul Keating says Defence is trying to 'vandalise the national estate' as many fight land sale
items.description: Opposition is growing to the federal government's plan to sell scores of defence properties to reduce maintenance and repair costs, as locals fight back.

items.title: UTS 'effectively silenced' student who complained of sexual harassment
items.description: The National Student Ombudsman takes aim at the University of Technology Sydney in one of its first major investigations, accusing the university of isolating a young complainant.

items.title: Deadline arrives for Sandilands to respond to misconduct claims
items.description: Almost one month on from the explosive argument between its star hosts, the Kyle and Jackie O Show is expected to learn its fate on Tuesday.

items.title: Sydney Swans take responsibility for Bondi tribute script change
items.description: The club says it takes full responsibility for a script change that removed references to the Jewish community during an opening round tribute to Bondi victims.

items.title: How to watch Matildas vs China in Women's Asian Cup semifinal
items.description: The Matildas are in the final four at the Women's Asian Cup, and take on the defending champion China in the first semifinal tonight. Here's how to follow the game at Perth Stadium.

items.title: Let your slow cooker do the work with these set-and-forget comfort meals
items.description: We've pulled together four lovely recipes that make weeknight meals a little easier (and quite budget friendly, too).

items.title: ABC Places quiz: Where in the world are we?
items.description: Today's ABC Places quiz features photos from 10 locations around the world. Your challenge is to guess where you are.

items.title: What is 'lifestyle creep' — and how can you avoid it?
items.description: If you tend to splurge on more indulgences any time you receive a pay rise, you may be suffering from lifestyle creep — and it could have a longstanding effect on your finances.

items.title: 'We don't talk about it enough': Mum makes emotional return to Super Netball
items.description: The world's best goal keeper has sparked an important conversation about postpartum depression in her return to the Super Netball league.

items.title: Duck hunters blame protesters for burning shooting shelters
items.description: Tasmanian duck hunters believe their shooting shelters, known as hides, are being burnt down by protesters, with 80 destroyed in the past four years.

items.title: A dead shark, sick surfers and the four-month wait to warn the public
items.description: The government knew a harmful toxin had been found in its algal bloom, but took months to update its health advice.

items.title: David Speirs says he is 'owning' his drug conviction as he chases a return to office
items.description: One-time Liberal opposition leader David Speirs is attempting a political comeback, but even he concedes it's a long shot after a very public downfall where he was convicted of supplying cocaine just over 10 months ago.

items.title: Matildas coy about star duo's chances of facing China in Asian Cup semi
items.description: Hayley Raso and Steph Catley are available for selection, but it remains to be seen what role they will have against China in Perth.

items.title: A third of all Victorian car thefts now involve key cloning devices
items.description: Police say criminals are able to steal certain push-button start models within 15 seconds, using key reprogramming devices bought online.

items.title: Mother was 'living beyond her means' during fake cancer scam, court hears
items.description: An Adelaide mother who faked her six-year-old son's cancer diagnosis to deceitfully raise money was "living the life of the rich and famous" despite serious financial struggles, a court has heard.
